chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Fadhalah ibn Ayub, from Abdullah ibn Zaid, from Ibn Abi Ya'foor who said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, told me:

Do not let people delude you against yourself, for that which is destined for you shall reach you in spite of them. And do not let the days pass you by with this and that, for surely there is One with you who records your deeds. And do not belittle any small good deed, for you shall see it tomorrow in a form that will please you. And do not underestimate any small evil deed, for you shall see it tomorrow in a form that will grieve you. And do good, for I have not seen anything more earnest in pursuit nor quicker in catching up than a good deed against an old sin.
Indeed, Allah, exalted is His name, says: 'Indeed, good deeds carry away evil deeds; that is a reminder for those who remember.'

key_terms.تستقل: To consider insignificant or belittle (root: q-l-l)
key_terms.حسنة: A good deed, a virtuous act
key_terms.يغرك: To delude, deceive, or mislead (root: gh-r-r)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the importance of small good and evil deeds?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), through a chain going back via Ibn Abi Ya'foor, delivers a comprehensive moral exhortation. He warns against being deceived by others and wasting time on trivial matters, reminds the listener that their deeds are being recorded, and emphasizes that no good or evil deed -- however small -- should be underestimated, as all will be seen on the Day of Judgment. He concludes by citing Quran 11:114 to affirm that good deeds erase bad ones.
word_analysis: And with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 3. And with the preceding chains of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Fadhalah ibn Ayub, from Abdullah ibn Zaid, from Ibn Abi Ya’foor who said: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon both, told me:

"Let not people delude you against yourself, for that which is your fate shall reach you in spite of them! And let not the days prevent you from this and that, for surely, with you is the One Who protects you! And do not belittle your little good deeds, for you shall see them tomorrow in a form, which will please you. And do not underestimate your little evil deeds, for you shall see them tomorrow in a form, which will grieve you. Do good deeds, for I have seen nothing quicker in pursuit of an old sin, so as to blot it out, than the good deed.
Surely, Allah says (in the Qur’an): ’Indeed, good deeds carry away the evil deeds; and that is a reminder for those who remember Allah.’(Hud, 11:114)"
